title: Governance lane: release criteria and gating for SSO / audit logs / SOC2 evidence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and operationalize a governance 'lane' that codifies release criteria, automated evidence checks, and rollback gates for any feature touching SSO/SAML, audit-log retention and SOC2 scope. Goal is to reduce manual gating, shorten compliance lead time, and ensure predictable release behavior for security-sensitive changes.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable checklist exists that maps feature changes to required evidence artifacts (configuration, logs, test results)
Automated pre-merge checks fail builds when key controls regress (SSO SAML metadata, login audit events, log retention policy)
Console release pipeline enforces gating: security signoff + artifact presence before canary/GA for private/dedicated deployments
Runbook and SLA for evidence retrieval created and validated with internal audit team
Operational dashboard shows pass/fail status per release with historical evidence links
tasks: Create canonical mapping document: feature -> required evidence artifacts
Define machine-checkable rules and implement as CI checks (ENG-4128)
Extend Console rollout workflow to require 'security gate' before canary (ENG-3951)
Build an evidence-collection Lambda for SOC2 artifacts and attach to release metadata
Coordinate with Audit/Legal to validate acceptance criteria and retention windows
Author internal runbook for incident + non-compliance remediation steps
Draft customer-facing release note template for security-sensitive changes
risks: Automation gaps may produce false positives and block releases (mitigate: staged rollout, opt-out for emergency fixes)
Backend dependency (log retention infra) has unplanned performance impact during evidence collection
Lack of cross-team alignment could delay signoffs (mitigate: weekly SLAs and escalation path)
If gates are too strict, developer velocity will suffer and teams may circumvent controls
